instruction: Use the ANSYS Fluent GUI to complete a two-dimensional steady laminar channel-flow analysis. Physical problem: Water flows through a straight two-dimensional rectangular channel. Geometry and coordinate system: - Use a 2D planar model in SI units. - The channel domain occupies 0 <= X <= 0.200 m and 0 <= Y <= 0.002 m. - Name the boundary zones exactly: X = 0 m: inlet; X = 0.200 m: outlet; Y = 0 m: bottom; Y = 0.002 m: top. Mesh: - Use a structured quadrilateral mesh. - Use 400 uniform divisions along the channel length. - Use 20 uniform divisions across the channel height. - The final mesh must contain 8000 quadrilateral cells. Material: - Fluid: water-liquid. - Density = 998.2 kg/m^3. - Dynamic viscosity = 0.001003 Pa*s. - Use constant material properties. Boundary conditions: - inlet: velocity-inlet with X velocity = 0.2 m/s and Y velocity = 0 m/s. - outlet: pressure-outlet with gauge pressure = 0 Pa. - top and bottom: stationary no-slip walls. Solver setup: - Pressure-based solver. - Steady formulation. - Laminar viscous model. - SIMPLE pressure-velocity coupling. - Pressure discretization: Second Order. - Momentum discretization: Second Order Upwind. - Hybrid initialization. - Run 500 iterations. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working directory. - Save the case file as C:\Users\user\Desktop\poiseuille_shear.cas. - Save the data file as C:\Users\user\Desktop\poiseuille_shear.dat. - Ensure both files contain the final solved state.
